_comment: Tag protection for published releases. Applied by hand, matched by name,
like the branch ruleset beside it.
THE PATTERN IS NARROW ON PURPOSE, AND THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT LINE IN
THE FILE. It matches refs/tags/v*.*.* and NOTHING ELSE, so it covers the
full version tags (v1.0.0, v1.4.2) and deliberately does NOT match the
bare major tag v1.
v1 must stay movable. Force-moving it is how a release is published to
every consumer, and force-moving it BACK is the only rollback that exists:
the sync path has no pull request, no staged rollout and no per-consumer
pin to edit, so a bad release is un-recalled until that tag moves. A
ruleset carrying refs/tags/v* (the shape shipped in the template home,
.github/.github/rulesets/protect-release-tags.json) blocks the update and
deletion of v1, which disables the release mechanism and the emergency
brake in the same rule, and it does it quietly: nothing fails until the
day someone needs to roll back.
The three rules make a PUBLISHED version tag immutable, which is what a
consumer pinning @v1.4.2 is promised: it cannot be deleted, cannot be
force-updated, and cannot be moved backwards.
THE ADMIN BYPASS IS PRESENT, unlike the variant this replaces. actor_id 5
is the repository-admin role. The no-bypass form is demonstrably not
enforced on this account (five v*.*.* tags were deleted from a repository
carrying exactly that rule), so the choice is between a rule that works
and a rule that lies about what it does.
name: Protect release tags (v*.*.*)
